suggestion: Keep both dated reads published side by side and stop describing either as current.
why_it_matters: The 13 November read carries 9 designations against today's 171. Treating a single read as current silently deletes 162 designations from any downstream count.
evidence_in_this_session: data/club_availability_20261115_dcf3b0cc.csv, column designations_20261113 versus the three designation columns for 15 November.
discovery_path: Already done in this tree; the fix needed on the canonical site is to label every injury table with its read time in the page heading.

suggestion: Retain the raw bytes of each capture, not only its metadata, once the terms review clears.
why_it_matters: Hashes that cannot be replayed do not satisfy the point-in-time gate and cannot support a backtest.
evidence_in_this_session: data/summary_dcf3b0cc.json publishes SHA-256 per artefact, but the underlying page bytes were not retained.
discovery_path: Resolve the price-data and terms questions already on the register, then turn on body retention in the monitor added by pull request 71.

suggestion: Capture the reserve and injured-reserve lists alongside each weekly report.
why_it_matters: Without them, 'not listed on the report' is read as 'available', which is false for every player on a reserve list.
evidence_in_this_session: 63 of today's 347 listed rows cannot be attached to a depth slot, and the reserve list is one of the reasons a name may be missing entirely.
discovery_path: Add a dated capture of the official transactions and reserve pages to the same schedule as the injury capture.

suggestion: Capture game-day inactive lists and snap counts before any depth feature ships.
why_it_matters: A replacement can only be confirmed, not suspected, once the inactive list and the snap share are available. Chart order alone is one step above inferring depth from a jersey number.
evidence_in_this_session: data/coverage_dcf3b0cc.csv: 284 of 347 listed players resolve to a chart row, and 55 of the 70 players ruled Out.
discovery_path: Start with the official game books for one week, verify the join, then widen.

suggestion: Adopt the schedule-page order as the single game-id convention and renumber the 13 November injury register.
why_it_matters: Three Week 10 ids name different fixtures in two published files, so a join on game_id attaches six clubs' rows to the wrong opponent. This session reproduced the disagreement from the hub's own display order.
discovery_path: Renumber the injury register, or drop game_id as a join key and join on club instead. The second is safer.

suggestion: Add a drift alarm pinned to expected row counts and required fields.
why_it_matters: Two reads two days apart differ by 51 rows and 162 designations. Without a pinned expectation the site publishes a stale table as if it were current.
discovery_path: Fail the build when a club that is playing publishes zero rows, or when the designation count falls below the previous read for the same week.

suggestion: Test the personnel features as an ablation rather than applying a fixed penalty.
why_it_matters: The brief explicitly rejects subtracting a fixed number of points for a missing starter. With 194 of 296 rows changing in two days, a fixed penalty would be fitted to one arbitrary snapshot.
discovery_path: Fit the identical model with and without the verified availability features on chronological holdouts and report the difference with its interval.

suggestion: Publish the deficiency matrix as a hypothesis register, not a finding.
why_it_matters: The available rank is 1 in 285 of 291 club groups, so the matrix currently says 'no mismatch' almost everywhere. That is a statement about the limits of chart order, not about the slate.
discovery_path: Label the matrix as a hypothesis to confirm against inactives and snap counts, and revisit once Q-DCF-03 and Q-DCF-04 are answered.

suggestion: Accumulate the n=28 weekly correlation before fitting anything.
why_it_matters: One week of 28 clubs produced no significant association. Publishing that honestly is more useful than waiting for a week that happens to look good.
evidence_in_this_session: data/correlation_dcf3b0cc.csv, seven pairs with intervals and p-values.
discovery_path: Compute the same seven pairs every week, store each week's row, and only test for signal once the sample is large enough to survive a multiplicity correction.
